policy.note: Asked once on first run (FEAT-001). No design tool holds these screens and the repo (shadcn/ui + tokens) is the design surface; screens are specified code-native in each feature's ui-design.md. Overridable per screen; switch to generate/register by connecting a design-tool MCP and re-running (re-verification registers tool designs after the fact).

SCR-WEB-002.name: Verify Email — Notice
SCR-WEB-002.notes: Arrival (default) state binds to POST /auth/register (201). The Resend control binds to POST /auth/verify/resend (FEAT-002); resend-sent renders the neutral 200. The rate-limited state is reinterpreted by FEAT-002 as a CLIENT-SIDE cooldown (RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS), not a server-throttle response — the resend contract is neutral (technical-design D3/D4), so the UI must not infer throttling from the response. See features/FEAT-002-verify-email/ui-design.md#scr-web-002--verify-email--notice-resend-binding-completed.

corrections: rate-limited state re-bound to a client-side cooldown to conform to FEAT-002's neutral resend contract (no server 429)

SCR-WEB-003.name: Verify Email — Result
SCR-WEB-003.notes: New web route /verify — target of the email verification link (${PUBLIC_APP_URL}/verify?token=…, FEAT-007 forward path). success routes to SCR-WEB-004 (FEAT-003). expired/invalid carry an email recovery form binding POST /auth/verify/resend; invalid folds in the already-verified case (UC-002 exc-3a) per technical-design D2.

SCR-WEB-004.name: Sign In
SCR-WEB-004.notes: Public auth zone, reusing the shared auth layout (centered 400px card + wordmark) from FEAT-001. 'error' folds the four designed login responses: 401 invalid_credentials (generic, no field highlight — no enumeration, FR-AUTH-010), 423 account_locked (FR-AUTH-019), 429 rate_limited (FR-AUTH-018), 400 validation_failed. 'unverified-prompt' is the 403 email_not_verified branch (FR-AUTH-007), reusing FEAT-002's POST /auth/verify/resend + client cooldown. Success (200) sets the session cookie via the web BFF (technical-design D6) and routes into the app-shell SCR-WEB-007.

SCR-WEB-005.name: Forgot Password
SCR-WEB-005.notes: Public auth zone (AuthShell). Served at /reset-password with no ?token=. Response is always the neutral 200 reset_requested; the 'submitted' state shows the same confirmation whether or not the email is registered (FR-AUTH-012, no enumeration). Shares the /reset-password route with SCR-WEB-006 (token-presence switch, ui-design D1).

SCR-WEB-006.name: Reset Password
SCR-WEB-006.notes: Public auth zone (AuthShell). Served at /reset-password?token=… (the worker-fixed reset-email link target). success reflects FR-AUTH-017 (other sessions signed out) and routes to /signin; invalid/expired map 400 token_invalid/token_expired with a 'request a new link' path; field-error is the 400 validation_failed password-policy case with the token NOT consumed (retry-friendly, technical-design D3).

SCR-WEB-007.name: App Shell — sidebar (lists, settings, sign-out)
SCR-WEB-007.notes: Cumulative entry for the app shell, extended once per shell-touching feature; the `source` locator points at the newest and most complete spec, and the earlier ones remain valid for their own parts: FEAT-004 sign-out control (features/FEAT-004-sign-out/ui-design.md#scr-web-007--app-shell-sign-out-control), FEAT-006 Settings nav item (features/FEAT-006-change-password/ui-design.md, D2), FEAT-009 lists section (current spec). FEAT-009 makes the sidebar the product's primary navigation: one `sidebar-nav-item` per list in `position` order with an activeTaskCount `badge` (hidden at zero — ui-design D2), a per-row `dropdown-menu` (rename / move up / move down / delete, with Delete absent on the default list — D1), and a 'New list' action, all opening SCR-WEB-011. Reorder is menu-driven, not drag-and-drop (D5) — design.md specifies a drag handle only on task-row, and §5 requires the move-up/down keyboard path regardless. FEAT-009 also implements the shell's `< md` full drawer that design.md §3 specified and FEAT-006 §8 recorded as unbuilt (D3), so 'ready' now covers both the desktop sidebar and the mobile drawer. No `empty` state exists by design: FR-LIST-003 guarantees every account has an Inbox. FEAT-010 is the entry's fourth extension: sidebar rows become LINKS to /lists/{id} and gain design.md's `sidebar-nav-item` selected state (primary-subtle bg + primary text + left accent bar, aria-current=page) for the open list, the drawer closes when a row is followed, and the count badge finally moves on its own now that tasks can be created; the `/` placeholder is replaced by SCR-WEB-008 rendering the default list (FEAT-010 technical-design D2). Delta spec: features/FEAT-010-create-task/ui-design.md#scr-web-007--app-shell-this-features-extension. Lucide icons remain unwired — controls are text/glyph with aria-labels (carried deviation, not an escalation). SCR-WEB-010's UC-004 tag is a likely source typo — no entry created for it. FEAT-011 is the entry's FIFTH extension (delta spec: features/FEAT-011-task-detail/ui-design.md#scr-web-007--app-shell-this-features-extension): the shell gains the DETAIL HOST its inventory entry always described — the `--size-detail-panel-width` (420px) right region SCR-WEB-010 slides into at >=lg, an overlay at md, full-viewport below md, and NOT RENDERED AT ALL when no task is open (no empty gutter). Esc closes it from anywhere in the shell and focus returns to the task-row that opened it (design.md §5). The earlier note that SCR-WEB-010 had no manifest entry is now superseded — FEAT-011 minted it against UC-010; the inventory's UC-004 tag on that screen remains a source typo. FEAT-019 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-019-realtime-sync/ui-design.md#scr-web-007--app-shell-this-features-extension): the shell mounts the sync island (<SyncProvider />, technical-design D7) — a client component that renders NOTHING and occupies no space; it is the product's only mount point that is authenticated-zone-only, which is why sync lives here and not in the root layout (no socket for a user who has no session). It consumes GET /realtime/token and never renders it: `{ enabled: false }` is the default configuration today (no Supabase project provisioned) and must not surface anywhere on the screen — it simply means the island runs the adaptive fallback schedule (technical-design D4). NO connection indicator, NO 'live' dot, NO last-updated timestamp (ui-design D1): design.md specifies no sync/connection/stale component, no FR or NFR asks for one, and D1 argues the product should not have one — so nothing was escalated either. A token-mint or socket failure is NOT a shell error state; the shell's `error` stays reserved for a failure to load the caller's lists. FEAT-008 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-008-profile/ui-design.md#scr-web-007--app-shell-this-features-extension): two changes, neither visual. (1) The Settings nav item's target moves from /settings/security to /settings/profile (technical-design D5) — ux-foundations' IA puts Profile & Preferences and Security & Account as siblings under Settings, and the preferences screen is the routinely-visited one; Security stays one click away via the settings sub-nav (ui-design D3). (2) The frame becomes the PREFERENCES HOST: it renders PreferencesProvider (timezone + theme + display name, server-fetched alongside the lists in one Promise.all) and ThemeSync, and it is where the one-time browser-timezone adoption PATCH fires when the profile reports timezone: null (technical-design AC-7). Like SyncProvider before it, this is authenticated-zone-only and renders nothing. The DISPLAY NAME IS DELIBERATELY NOT SHOWN IN THE SIDEBAR (ui-design D8): no FR asks for it and the shell has no identity block, so adding one would be a shell redesign needing its own ux pass. Sidebar appearance is unchanged in both themes — the selected nav item measures 5.47:1 light / 6.69:1 dark. FEAT-015 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-015-search/ui-design.md#scr-web-007--app-shell-this-features-extension): the sidebar gains a Search affordance above the smart-view items — a real `button` with an accessible name ('Search tasks') styled as the `command-search` field — and the shell becomes the OVERLAY'S MOUNT POINT and the owner of its global Ctrl/Cmd+K shortcut (ui-design D1/D6). Search is reachable from every authenticated screen with one mount, which is why it lives here rather than on the list view. The shell's own contract bindings are unchanged; the overlay it opens binds to GET /search.

SCR-WEB-008.notes: The product's main working surface, served at /lists/{id} and at / for the caller's default list (technical-design D2) — one component, two routes. `task-row` is realized as a DELIBERATE SUBSET (ui-design D2): title only. The complete-checkbox (FEAT-012), due-date chip and priority dot (FEAT-011), row-click to SCR-WEB-010 (FEAT-011) and drag handle (FEAT-014) are omitted rather than faked — a control that looks live but isn't is worse than an absent one; each later feature ADDS to this row rather than reworking it. The completed section is specified but renders only when non-empty (D3), since nothing can complete a task until FEAT-012. The composer is the empty state's primary action rather than a second button (D4). `loading` is covered by server rendering, not a skeleton — recorded honestly. `not-found` is a supplementary state beyond the inventory's four: /lists/{id} for an unknown OR unowned id gets one uniform in-shell alert, never a disclosure of which (technical-design §3.1). FEAT-011 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-011-task-detail/ui-design.md#scr-web-008--list-view-this-features-extension): `task-row` gains two of its four deferred parts — the due-date chip (absent entirely when dueAt is null; carries the word 'Overdue' plus the danger treatment when task.isOverdue) and the priority dot (`--priority-*`, with an aria-label; NOT rendered for 'none', since the default state is the absence of a mark). The row also becomes the click target for detail, opening SCR-WEB-010, as design.md's task-row always specified. `quick-add` reaches its full design.md form: two inline affordances opening the SAME due-date-picker and priority-selector the detail panel uses (ui-design D4), each resetting after a successful create, with Enter still creating on title alone so NFR-USE-001's one-field path is unchanged. Still deferred: the complete-checkbox (FEAT-012) and drag handle (FEAT-014). The recorded responsive gap below (mobile bottom-anchored composer) is UNCHANGED by this feature — controls were added inside the composer without moving it. FEAT-012 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-012-complete-reopen/ui-design.md#scr-web-008--list-view-this-features-extension): `task-row` gains the complete-`checkbox` — the THIRD of FEAT-010 D2's four deferrals, leaving only the drag handle (FEAT-014). It is a real <input type=checkbox> so Space toggles complete (design.md §5's own keyboard rule) and it is a SIBLING of the row link, never nested inside it (technical-design D6: an interactive control inside an anchor is invalid markup with undefined activation). Optimistic with rollback on failure (D1): only the box's state is optimistic — the row does not change section until the server confirms, so a failure never yanks a row across a section boundary. The completed section becomes a collapsed <details>/<summary> disclosure carrying its count (FR-TASK-011; technical-design D5) — native, so keyboard operability and the expanded/collapsed announcement come free with zero client JS; still absent entirely when nothing is completed. Completed rows take NO `--color-surface-sunken` hover tint (D3, measured: muted text on that tint is 4.34:1, under §5's 4.5:1 at `body` size). A list whose only tasks are completed is not 'empty' — it shows the collapsed section and suppresses the empty-state block, a composition FEAT-010's spec could not previously reach. FEAT-013 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-013-delete-restore/ui-design.md#scr-web-008--list-view-this-features-extension): a confirmed delete removes the task-row from its section and drops the header and sidebar counts, server-rendered via router.refresh() with no removal animation (design.md specifies none). The undo snackbar is design.md §4's toast in its undo-snackbar variant — --color-surface + hairline --color-border + --radius-lg + --shadow-lg, bottom-right at >=md / bottom-center below, 'Task deleted.' plus an 'Undo' button-tertiary (--color-primary: 5.47:1 light, 9.15:1 dark on the toast surface), ~7s auto-dismiss PAUSED on hover or focus (D3), announced role=status/aria-live=polite and never taking focus. It overlays the list without reflowing it, survives the list becoming empty (that is when undo matters most), and is mounted above the whole shell (technical-design D6) so a failed list refresh cannot take the recovery affordance with it. Undo restores by POST /tasks/{id}/restore then router.refresh() — never by replaying client state (D2). z-index 60, the layer lists-nav's toast already uses. FEAT-019 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-019-realtime-sync/ui-design.md#scr-web-008--list-view-this-features-extension): no new element, no new region, no badge — what changes is WHEN the existing composition re-renders. Rows, sections, the header count and the sidebar badges can now change from another device's write with no interaction here. NO arrival or departure treatment (ui-design D1/D5): a remotely-created row appears exactly as a locally-created one does — no flash, no highlight, no slide, no 'new' marker — because design.md §5 forbids conveying information by motion alone and animating nothing satisfies prefers-reduced-motion by construction. A background refresh NEVER shows the `loading` state (no spinner/skeleton/dimming for an update the user did not request) and a FAILED background refresh is silent and retried, never the `error` state — `error` stays reserved for a failed user-initiated load. `empty` and the completed-only composition are newly reachable with no interaction (the last active task completed or deleted elsewhere) and render exactly as already specified. `not-found` is NEWLY REACHABLE WITHOUT NAVIGATION (the open list deleted elsewhere) and is NOT redirected away from (ui-design D3) — the existing uniform in-shell alert renders in place with the sidebar still offering every other list. A row that vanishes from a remote delete carries NO undo affordance: undo is local to the deleting device (FEAT-013 D7, ui-design D4) and the content-free signal means this device does not even know what was deleted. The refresh must preserve focus, scroll, uncommitted composer text, open overlays, the undo snackbar's remaining timer and in-flight optimistic controls (ui-design D2 — the enumerated preservation list is this feature's real user-visible contract). Both recorded gaps below are CARRIED UNCHANGED: this feature adds no toast and moves no composer.

SCR-WEB-010.name: Task Detail
SCR-WEB-010.notes: Minted by FEAT-011 — the screen the inventory has listed since ux-foundations and the 'detail host' SCR-WEB-007 was always specified to have. Route-first (ui-design D1): /tasks/{id} is a real deep-linkable URL, presented as design.md §3's shell detail host — 420px right slide-in at >=lg, overlay at md, full-screen below md. Edits save PER FIELD ON COMMIT with no Save button (D2), which is what technical-design D4's partial PATCH exists for; each control owns its loading/error state and a failed save KEEPS the typed value. Read-only in this slice by design: the status line (complete/reopen is FEAT-012), and the LIST — design.md's task-detail-panel spec lists a `list-picker` but no FR authorizes moving a task between lists and the PATCH contract rejects `listId`, so it is NOT built and is surfaced as a candidate requirements amendment (D3). Priority shows a dot AND a text label (design.md §5: never colour alone). Overdue renders the word 'Overdue', never colour alone, from the server's `isOverdue` — the screen never re-implements the rule. The due-date-picker and priority-selector are shared with SCR-WEB-008's quick-add (D4), built once. Timezone for input interpretation and display is the BROWSER's until FEAT-008 stores one (technical-design D1/§8); the wire is always UTC. `loading` is covered by server rendering, not a skeleton — recorded honestly. `not-found` is a supplementary state beyond the inventory's four: unknown, unowned and soft-deleted ids get one uniform in-shell alert, never a disclosure of which. The inventory's SCR-WEB-010 -> UC-004 tag is a source typo (third artifact to record it); this screen realizes UC-010, with UC-011/012 attaching via FEAT-012/013. FEAT-012 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-012-complete-reopen/ui-design.md#scr-web-010--task-detail-this-features-extension): the read-only status line becomes the status CONTROL — the same complete-`checkbox` as the list row, labelled 'Mark complete' / 'Completed <date>', so there is one target and one keyboard path (Space) on both screens. Because one TaskDetail component serves both the intercepted panel and the full-page route (FEAT-011 D1), the control lands in both with no second spec. The overdue chip disappears on completion from the server's `isOverdue`, never a local rule. Still absent: delete (FEAT-013) and the `list-picker` (no FR — FEAT-011 D3, unchanged). At < md the control sits above the fold: completing is this screen's most common action and must not require a scroll. FEAT-013 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-013-delete-restore/ui-design.md#scr-web-010--task-detail-this-features-extension): the panel gains design.md §4's `button-danger` 'Delete task' as the LAST control in DOM order, below the editing fields behind --space-6 and a hairline rule, and NEW state `confirming` — a confirm-dialog (title 'Delete this task?', the task's title in the body, 'You'll be able to undo this for a few seconds.', button-secondary Cancel + button-danger Delete, confirm takes initial focus, trap + Esc + scrim, focus restored to the delete control). NOTHING is written on any path but confirm (AC-9b): this is NFR-USE-002's literal reading, ruled on by the product owner 2026-07-29 (technical-design D2), and it is why ux-foundations §A5/Flow 3 — which still draw the snackbar-only flow — owe an amendment. A failed delete keeps the dialog open with an inline-alert in --color-danger-text and the task still in the list; it never closes as though it worked. The dialog is a SECOND local dialog, not a refactor of list-dialog.tsx (D1) — the shared confirm-dialog design.md §4 describes is a foundations item once FEAT-018 becomes its third caller. Below md the control sits at the end of the scrollable content rather than pinned — the inverse of FEAT-012's above-the-fold rule for the checkbox, and for the same reason: frequency. FEAT-019 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-019-realtime-sync/ui-design.md#scr-web-010--task-detail-this-features-extension): the panel re-renders on the same router.refresh() as the list behind it (the route's slots re-render together), in both presentations. `viewing` may update field values from another device with no treatment marking them changed (ui-design D1). `editing`: a background refresh must NEVER overwrite a field being edited — FEAT-011 D2's per-field-on-commit controls hold their own uncommitted value and that value WINS until commit or revert; no merge prompt and no 'changed elsewhere' warning, because the PATCH contract is last-write-wins and inventing a conflict UI would fork a decision the API did not make (ui-design D2). `confirming`: the delete confirm dialog STAYS OPEN across a refresh with its focus trap and focused control intact; if the task was deleted elsewhere meanwhile, the confirm's DELETE is idempotent and returns the original deletedAt (FEAT-013 D3), so the user is never told their action failed when the outcome holds. `not-found` is NEWLY REACHABLE WITHOUT NAVIGATION and is the more disruptive of the two: the open task deleted elsewhere renders the existing uniform not-found alert IN PLACE — the panel DOES NOT CLOSE ITSELF (ui-design D3), since closing reads as the app dismissing the user's context unasked; the user closes it and focus returns to the originating row as it already does. No background refresh shows `loading`; a failed one is silent.

Third instance of one pattern: FEAT-012 filed the identical finding for the checkbox's 'white check' glyph, and the amendment that landed corrected §4's `checkbox` but left `button-danger` alone. DOCUMENTATION-ONLY — no token value changes and no shipped code changes (list-dialog.tsx already uses --color-on-primary, 6.12:1 dark). Proposal: replace 'white text' with --color-on-primary in §4's button-danger entry and add the pairing to §8's quick reference. Screens are specified against the proposal; blocks no structure, state or binding.

NOT AN ESCALATION, RECORDED FOR ROUTING — five shipped sites still put --color-danger on --color-danger-subtle at small (3.95:1, the DEF-003 pairing): app/signup/page.tsx:89-91, app/signin/page.tsx:128-130, app/reset-password/page.tsx:46-48, components/lists-nav.tsx:117-119, components/list-dialog.tsx:196-198. DEF-003 fixed list-view-failure.tsx and DEF-004 swept the chip/badge pairing; neither swept the inline-alert instances. This is a defect on verified features — maintenance route (one ledger row + one web-tier pass, the DEF-005 shape), not FEAT-013 rework. FEAT-013's own dialog is specified with --color-danger-text regardless.

SCR-WEB-011.name: Create/Edit List
SCR-WEB-011.notes: One dialog screen carrying three UC-008 paths (create, rename, delete-confirm); no route of its own (ui-design D4). Delete uses design.md's `confirm-dialog`, which the system names for 'delete list' by name (NFR-USE-002); the confirmation quantifies the loss from ListSummary.taskCount (technical-design D8) and offers NO undo — list deletion hard-deletes its tasks (technical-design D4). The 409 list_not_deletable branch is rendered but unreachable through the UI, because the Inbox row omits Delete entirely (ui-design D1).

SCR-WEB-012.name: Search
SCR-WEB-012.notes: The product's first OVERLAY surface and its first incrementally-loading one. Mounted in shell-frame, not a route (ui-design D1): search must be reachable from every authenticated screen without pushing the user's current list out of view or into back-history — the consequence being that a search has no URL and cannot be linked or restored, recorded rather than discovered. Composition: design.md `dialog` > search input + two filter `select`s + results + a Load-more `button-secondary`. ESCALATION FILED AND RESOLVED 2026-07-31 (design.md §9 amendment): design.md §4's `command-search` sketch said results were 'grouped by list', which could not hold alongside this feature's contract — keyset pagination fragments groups across pages (FR-SRCH-009), grouping contradicts the newest-first order (technical-design D2), and FR-SRCH-002 asks for per-result ATTRIBUTION, not grouping. The amendment was approved and applied, so the per-row list chips this screen specifies ARE the design system's rule now, not a provisional deviation from it. A result row is a documented SUBSET of `task-row` (D2): every read affordance (title, list chip, due chip, priority dot, completed treatment) and NEITHER write control (no complete-checkbox, no drag handle) — the 'omit rather than fake' rule FEAT-010 ui-design D2 set. Due chip and priority dot are the EXISTING task-meta components, so a due date reads identically here and in the list view (zone-aware via useTimeZone). Filters are `select`s with an explicit 'Any' (= parameter not sent), not chips: the system has no toggle-chip or segmented control and minting one for a single consumer would be an amendment bought for one use (ui-design D3, the same judgement FEAT-008 D6 made about a combobox). Pagination is Load-more, not numbered pages (the cursor is opaque) and not infinite scroll (a keyboard user never reaches the trigger) — D4. idle and empty are distinct BY CONSTRUCTION: idle has no criteria to echo, which is the client half of technical-design D6. Query debounced ~250ms with out-of-order responses discarded, and previous results are NOT cleared while a new request is in flight (D5). Error state uses --color-danger-text on the danger tint, never --color-danger (the 3.95:1 DEF-003/DEF-006 pairing).

escalations: RESOLVED 2026-07-31 by the design.md §9 amendment. design.md §4 `command-search` said results were 'grouped by list'; unbuildable alongside keyset pagination (FR-SRCH-009) and the newest-first order (technical-design D2), and FR-SRCH-002 asks for per-row attribution instead. The component line now specifies per-result labelling and says the overlay renders the server's order without regrouping. Description correction only — no component forked, no token changed. This screen's spec was already written to the amended rule and is unchanged by it.

SCR-WEB-013.name: Settings — Profile & Preferences
SCR-WEB-013.notes: Authenticated settings zone (app shell), served at /settings/profile; the sidebar's Settings nav item now targets THIS screen and Security & Account (SCR-WEB-014) becomes its sibling, reached through the new settings sub-nav (ui-design D3) — technical-design D5. Four field blocks in one card: email as STATIC TEXT (not a disabled input — ui-design D4; FR-PROF-001 makes it read-only), display name (input + explicit Save), timezone (native select with optgroups, options from the BROWSER's Intl.supportedValuesOf — ui-design D6), theme (radio group: Light / Dark / Match system). Selects and radios save ON CHANGE, the text field on an explicit Save (ui-design D7); each control PATCHes only its own field, which is what the partial-patch contract (technical-design D6) exists for. TWO UI-SIDE READINGS OF CONTRACT STATES, recorded rather than left implicit: (1) a BLANK display-name field sends `null` (unset → derived default), never `""` (which the contract rejects) — ui-design D5; UC-007 alt 3a's error path stays reachable via too-long input, and the `""` rejection is enforced at the API. Same shape as FEAT-002's reinterpretation of SCR-WEB-002's rate-limited state. (2) The theme applies OPTIMISTICALLY to :root on change and reverts with the form-level error if the PATCH fails (ui-design D1) — it is not a preview widget. FIRST SCREEN IN THE PRODUCT TO RENDER THE DARK THEME: all nine pairings measured in both themes before writing (ui-design D2 carries the table), all ≥ 4.5:1; no correction, no amendment. Form-level errors use --color-danger-subtle + --color-danger-text, never --color-danger on that tint (the 3.95:1 DEF-003/DEF-006 pairing).

SCR-WEB-014.name: Settings — Security & Account
SCR-WEB-014.notes: Authenticated settings zone (app shell), served at /settings/security; reached from the new sidebar 'Settings' nav item (SCR-WEB-007 entry extended). Pure navigation hub — consumes no endpoint, so no loading/empty/error states apply (not gaps); an unresolved session redirects to /signin server-side (ui-design D4). Renders one list-row today (Change password → SCR-WEB-015); Export data (SCR-WEB-016, FEAT-017) and Delete account (SCR-WEB-017, FEAT-018) add rows to this same entry later. FEAT-008 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-008-profile/ui-design.md#scr-web-014--settings--security--account-this-features-extension): gains the settings sub-nav above its h1, with 'Security & account' carrying aria-current=page. This is required rather than cosmetic — FEAT-008 moves the sidebar's Settings target to /settings/profile, so without the sub-nav this screen would become unreachable. The sub-nav is a semantic <nav><ul><li><a> styled with design.md's `tabs` treatment, NOT shadcn Tabs (whose semantics are same-page panels, and these are routes — ui-design D3): a composition of existing treatments, not a new component. The card, its rows and its copy are otherwise untouched.

SCR-WEB-015.name: Change Password
SCR-WEB-015.notes: Authenticated settings zone, served at /settings/security/password — the first guarded form. 'error' covers three server failures on one screen: 400 current_password_invalid on the currentPassword field (UC-006 alt 3a), 400 validation_failed on newPassword (policy, alt 3b), and 429 rate_limited as a form-level alert; typed input is preserved in all three (NFR-REL-004). 'success' keeps the user signed in on the rotated cookie and names the FR-AUTH-017 consequence (other devices signed out) — no bounce to /signin (ui-design D3). 'unauthenticated' is a supplementary state beyond the inventory's three: a 401 on submit routes to /signin (ui-design D4).

SCR-WEB-018.name: First-run / Onboarding
SCR-WEB-018.notes: Not a route: it is the state SCR-WEB-008 renders at / for a brand-new account (ui-design D1). Trigger is explicit so implementation doesn't guess — the caller has EXACTLY ONE list (a single isDefault entry from GET /lists) AND it has no tasks; any other empty list, including the Inbox once a second list exists, gets SCR-WEB-008's generic empty state. First-run is about the account, not the list. On the first successful create it becomes SCR-WEB-008 'populated' — the transition is the onboarding's completion, with nothing to dismiss. Shares SCR-WEB-008's bindings; owns no endpoint.
